我们的预期寿命变化方程的一种等价写法是
ΔL ≈ avg(ΔHR) × L̄,
其中 L̄ 仍然表示"死亡时的预期寿命"（美国男性为 12.93 年），avg(ΔHR) 是风险变化的加权平均值，权重来自不同年龄段的 P(t) × L(t) 敏感度曲线。8 虽然这条敏感度曲线不是恒定的，但也不算太弯曲。直观地说，它对 50 到 90 岁之间的年龄段赋予了很大的权重，对 20 到 50 岁之间的年龄段赋予稍小的权重，而对其他年龄段的权重很小。9
所以情况还不算太糟。但让我们记住最初的问题：你在论文中看到类似 HR = 0.90 这样的数字，想把它换算为预期寿命的变化。如果真实的风险比是恒定的，那没问题。但如果它不恒定，那么 HR = 0.90 这个数字到底意味着什么？
论文中的数字
遗憾的是，你几乎永远看不到潜在的随时间变化的 HR(t)，因为几乎没有足够的数据来估计它。因此，计算加权平均值 avg(ΔHR) 几乎是不可能的。实际上，你手上可能只有论文里的一个单一数字。我们把这个数字称为 est(HR)。最直接的做法是将这个变化量代入上面的等式来替代 avg(ΔHR)，从而将预期寿命的变化近似为
ΔL ≈ est(ΔHR) × L̄.
同样，你可以直接把 est(ΔHR) = 1-est(HR) 看作是风险的估计减少量。不过，还是那句话，如果你能接受对数的话，我更建议你使用对数。10 那么问题来了：这准确吗？est(ΔHR) 和 avg(ΔHR) 有多接近？
那么，人们实际上是如何估计论文中那些标量风险率数值的呢？不管怎样，他们都是将不同年龄的风险信息聚合到一个数字中。但怎么聚合的呢？嗯，这很复杂。但如果有大量数据，你可以证明估计的标量风险率大约是11
est(HR) ≈ Πₜ HR(t)ᵖ⁽ᵗ⁾.
（请原谅这糟糕的排版。）也就是说，估计的风险率是依赖于年龄的风险率的几何平均值，并按每个年龄的死亡概率进行加权。由此可得12，风险的估计变化量大约为
est(ΔHR) ≈ ∑ₜ P(t) ΔHR(t).

因此，理想情况下，我们会使用 avg(ΔHR) 来估计预期寿命，它是根据权重 P(t) × L(t) 对变化量 ΔHR(t) 求平均。但我们做不到这一点，因为我们无法获取 ΔHR(t) 的数值。我们能做的是读取论文中的风险率数值，将其称为 est(HR)，然后计算变化量 est(ΔHR)。上面的等式表明，如果你这样做，你实际上是（近似地）仅根据权重 P(t) 对变化量 ΔHR(t) 进行了隐式平均。
avg(ΔHR) 使用的“正确”权重与 est(ΔHR) 隐式使用的“错误”权重并不相同。但它们也没有太大的区别。这是 P(t) × L(t)，也就是我们希望用来计算 avg(ΔHR) 并准确估计预期寿命变化的权重：
这是 P(t)，也就是如果我们从论文中取风险率数值并计算 est(ΔHR) 时，你隐式使用的权重：
它们是不同的。具体来说，后者的权重给了 80-95 岁的人更多的权重，而给了 20-50 岁的人更少的权重。但它们并没有天壤之别。
数学讲够了，让我们试一试
首先，假设存在某种干预措施，能使所有年龄段的风险降低 HR(t)=0.9。
结果如下：

让我解释一下这里发生了什么。我做了一个模拟器，输入美国男性在不同年龄死亡概率的精算数据。由此，通过简单的电子表格计算就可以得出预期寿命 L。13 然后我应用了一个风险率来改变每个年龄的死亡概率，并重新运行模拟器来计算新的预期寿命 L’ 和准确的差值 ΔL。接着我展示了 ΔL 的两种近似值：第一种是使用 avg(ΔHR) 的“理想近似”，我把它加进来主要是为了证明我的数学是正确的。最后，我展示了如果你实际拟合一个 Cox 比例风险模型，并使用得出的数值计算 est(ΔHR) 所得到的近似值。这相当于你代入论文中数字所得到的结果。
因此，在上述恒定风险率 HR = 0.90 的情况下，这两种近似都非常好。如果你换成其他常数，情况依然如此。
如果风险率发生变化会怎样？起初，你可能会认为类似这样的情况会非常成问题：
但其实基本没问题：
之所以说这没问题，是因为风险比（hazard ratio）的变化相对“高频”，这意味着它们在局部范围内会被平均掉。为了证明这一点，假设每个1年区间的风险比是随机选择的：
这样近似的效果甚至会更好：
真正会引发问题的是，风险比在年轻人和老年人之间是否存在系统性变化。例如，假设某种干预措施对新生儿无效，但随着年龄增长，其效果会逐渐增强：
如果能够计算的话，我的“理想近似”仍然会非常准确。（在现实世界中，你是无法计算的。）但是，如果直接使用论文中的数值，则会导致高估：
出现这种情况是因为 est(ΔHR) 隐含地受 P(t) 加权，而 P(t) 严重向老年人倾斜；相反，我们更希望使用类似于 avg(ΔHR) 的值，它由 P(t) × L(t) 进行加权，向老年人倾斜的程度相对较低。即便如此，误差也并不算太糟。
然而，直接套用论文中的风险比也有可能对预期寿命做出极其不准确的估计。其中一种情况是，某项干预措施对85至95岁的人群效果奇佳，但对其他任何人都没有作用：
此时，风险比恰好在了 est(ΔHR) 权重最大的年龄段表现出色，从而导致它极其严重地高估了对预期寿命的影响：
另一个堪称噩梦的情况是，某项干预措施一开始是有害的，但到了老年阶段却变得有益：
在这种情况下，使用论文中的数值甚至无法给出符号正确的估计值。
这确实很糟糕。但我认为大多数干预措施可能并非如此？我的猜测是，大多数真实的干预措施会随年龄产生一定的变化，但这种变化是渐进的，且不会改变作用方向（即正负号）。在这些情况下，很难找到直接套用论文数值会导致偏差超过30%左右的例子。如果你不信，大可一试。14
总结
如果我们是其他物种，将风险比转化为预期寿命的变化可能会非常困难。但对于富裕国家的现代人来说，存在三个幸运的巧合：
死亡风险的分布恰好使得你可以通过不同年龄段风险比的简单加权和来近似计算预期寿命的变化，同时忽略交互作用。
人们用来估计标量风险比的统计方法，同样可以近似为不同年龄段风险比的加权和，且忽略交互作用。
估算预期寿命所需的权重（来自第1点）与计算风险比数值时隐含使用的权重（来自第2点）并不相同。但它们相当接近。
这些事实证明了以下做法的合理性：从论文中获取估计的风险比数值 HR，并将预期寿命的变化近似为 ΔL ≈ ln(1/HR) × 12.93 年；或者，如果风险比接近于1且你讨厌对数，可以近似为 ΔL ≈ (1-HR) × 12.93 年。
12.93 年这个数值是针对美国男性的。它是 Keyfitz 熵（0.17）和基准预期寿命（75.8年）的乘积。在其他人群中，该数值会有所不同。
如果真实的潜在风险比：
……在各年龄段保持不变，那么上述近似将极其准确。
……随着人们年龄的增长而降低，该近似就会高估 ΔL。也就是说，它会让有益的干预措施看起来比实际更好，而让有害的干预措施看起来比实际的危害要小。
……随着人们年龄的增长而增加，这种近似法会低估 ΔL。也就是说，它会让有益的干预措施看起来不如实际那么有效，也会让有害的干预措施看起来比实际更糟。
但只要真实的基础风险比（hazard ratio）不是太离谱，误差在任何方向上可能都不会超过 30% 左右。

最后，有两个主要的注意事项：首先，上述讨论假设风险比是通过对所有年龄段的人进行试验来估计的。通常，est(ΔHR) 会隐含地根据试验中基准人群在各年龄段的死亡人数，对不同年龄段赋予相应的权重。如果设定了（比如说）50岁的最低年龄限制，影响不会太大，因为 P(t) 的大部分质量本来就分布在50岁以上。但如果最低年龄限制是70岁，或者最高年龄限制是50岁，且在那些未被观察到的年龄段中真实的风险比有所不同，那就会产生巨大的差异。

其次，这些是对人口预期寿命的估计。但你并不是一个群体。在某种意义上，你的基因和生活方式意味着你有自己的“个人 Keyfitz 熵”，这反映了如果你度过数百万次随机的人生，你的死亡时间分布会有多分散。如果你安全驾驶、使用空气净化器、饮食健康、坚持锻炼并且不吸烟，这可能意味着你的个人预期寿命高于平均水平。但这也很可能意味着你的个人 Keyfitz 熵低于平均水平。15 因此，如果你通过多吃纤维或其他方式进一步改善生活方式，即使这对你和其他人产生相同的风险比，它仍然可能导致预期寿命的增幅较小，其原因与相同的风险比在人类身上产生的寿命变化比小鼠更小是一样的。我们真正需要的是一些足够强大的干预措施，以打破这些近似背后的数学限制，将我们从 Keyfitz 的桎梏中解放出来。
我知道，我知道，你关心的是生活质量，而不仅仅是生命的年数。我同意，某种衡量健康和活力的指标，也许是伤残调整生命年（DALY）或质量调整生命年（QALY），会更好。但这些很难估计，因此很少被报道。无论如何，在实践中，大多数能让你更有活力的干预措施往往也能让你活得更久，反之亦然，所以关注预期寿命也还不错。 ↩
在这个模型中，生命的天数服从几何分布，其中 p =（子弹数量）/（弹膛数量）。因此，平均预期寿命为 1/p 天，即（弹膛数量）/（子弹数量）天。如果有 54,786 个弹膛和 2 颗子弹，算出来就是 75 年。如果你减到 1 颗子弹，那么预期寿命就会增加到 150 年。 ↩
如果在史前部落群体中，某种干预措施能降低 60 岁及以上人群的死亡率，这并不会大幅提高预期寿命，因为大多数人活不到 60 岁。但与史前部落群体相比，我们实际上已经大幅降低了年轻时的死亡率。因此，在今天，降低 60 岁及以上人群的死亡率将大大提高预期寿命。 ↩
你可能觉得这很愚蠢。如果你只是打算假设相对风险（relative risk）是恒定的，那为什么还要把它转换成风险比（hazard ratio）呢？这不是毫无意义吗？其实不然。还记得相对风险在足够长的试验中总是趋近于 1.0 吗，因为治疗组和对照组的所有人最终都会离开人世？而恒定的风险比就不会发生这种情况。 ↩
通常（虽然并非总是如此），使用 ΔHR(t) = ln(1/HR(t)) 会更好。例如，这能正确反映出，如果所有风险比（hazard ratio）都降至零，那么预期寿命就会趋于无穷大，太棒了。对于接近 1 的风险比，这两种近似几乎完全相同，因为当 r 接近 1 时，ln(1/r) ≈ (1-r)。所以，如果你对对数感到恐惧，但不管怎样还是读到了这条脚注的结尾，你也不会错过太多东西。↩
这一论点存在一定程度的循环论证。它假设与预期寿命的变化相比，风险比在不同物种之间具有更好的可迁移性。这可能是正确的，但这将是一个经验性/生物学层面的事实，而非逻辑所能保证的。↩
要理解这一点，请注意 ΔL ≈ ∑ₜ ΔHR(t) × P(t) × L(t) = L̄ × ∑ₜ ΔHR(t) × (P(t) × L(t) / L̄) = L̄ × avg(ΔHR)。↩
事实证明，一个相当不错的近似是 avg(ΔHR) ≈ 0.27 × avg₂₀₋₅₀(ΔHR) + 0.73 × avg₅₀₋₉₀(ΔHR)，其中 avg₂₀₋₅₀(ΔHR) 表示 20 至 50 岁期间变化量的简单平均值，而 avg₅₀₋₉₀(ΔHR) 表示 50 至 90 岁期间的简单平均值。↩
也就是说，最好使用 est(ΔHR) = ln(1/est(HR))。当 est(HR) 接近 1 时，该式接近于 1-est(HR)。↩

如果有无限的数据，典型的方法可简化为求解方程 ∑ₜ (P(t) + P’(t)) × π(t, HR) = ∑ₜ P’(t) 中的 HR。这里，P’(t) 是应用风险比后在年龄 t 时死亡的概率，而 π(t, HR) 是指如果死亡发生在时间 t，其属于治疗组的概率。当然，死亡属于治疗组的真实概率是 P’(t) / (P(t) + P’(t))。标准的“Cox 比例风险”模型假设风险比是恒定的，因此用基于模型的比率替换了这个原始比例，即 π(t, HR) = S’(t) × HR / (S(t) + S’(t) × HR)。这反映了这样一个事实：在年龄 t 时，对照组中有比例为 S(t) 的人存活，且每个人都有 μ(t) 的死亡几率，因此 P(t) = S(t) × μ(t)。同时，治疗组中有比例为 S’(t) 的人存活，每个人都有 HR × μ(t) 的死亡几率，这意味着 P’(t) = S’(t) × HR × μ(t)。如果你将这些关于 P(t) 和 P’(t) 的等式代入上面的第二个等式，μ(t) 这一因子会方便地抵消，从而得到所写的 π(t, HR)。实际上，风险比的作用就是将死亡归因于治疗组还是对照组。现在，如果真实的时变 HR(t) 接近 1，那么可以证明，估计的风险比 est(HR) 近似满足 ln(est(HR)) ≈ ∑ₜ P(t) ln(HR(t))。↩

几何平均数等价于以下条件：ln(est(HR)) ≈ ∑ₜ P(t) ln(HR(t))。使用 ΔHR(t) = ln(1/HR(t)) 和 *est(ΔHR)=ln(1/est(HR)) 这一“更好”的近似，可以得出 est(ΔHR) ≈ ∑ₜ P(t) ΔHR(t)。由于当 HR(t) 接近 1 时这些式子几乎相同，因此你也可以使用 est(ΔHR) = 1-est(HR) 和 ΔHR(t)=1-HR(t) 来解释同一个方程。↩
这个模拟器假设人们存活的年数为整数。当然，这在现实中并不成立，但这使得模拟器更容易实现和理解，并且在实践中几乎没有区别。↩
在模拟中，“true ΔL”指的是我上文提到的“exact ΔL”，而“approximation (log)”指的是“ideal approximation”，“Cox fitted”指的是“Use number from paper”。↩
鉴于现代人类死亡率的分布情况，即使你的健康生活方式能在所有年龄段将死亡率降低一个恒定的比例，这仍然会起到降低 Keyfitz 熵的作用。↩

blocks.text: I ran across a geometry theorem with the following diagram.
The theorem corresponding to the diagram is interesting, but I found reproducing the diagram more interesting.
The segment AB is a diameter and the line CD is perpendicular to the diameter.
Assume the outer circle is a unit circle. I guessed C = (cos(1), sin(1)) and made the following diagram.
I guessed the value of C by eyeballing it, but in retrospect this would have been a convenient value for the creator of the original diagram to have chosen.

Drawing the blue circle inscribed in the triangle was easy using the equations for the center and radius from this post. Drawing the other two circles, the green and orange circles, was harder. They are also inscribed circles, but not inscribed in a triangle. They’re inscribed in a three-sided figure with two perpendicular sides and a circular arc.

The radius r of the green circle is the distance from the center of the circle to each of its tangent lines. Also, the distance from the origin to the center of the circle must be 1 − r. This is enough information to set up a quadratic equation for r. The same reasoning applies to the orange circle.
The original diagram comes from [1] and the theorem it illustrates says the diameter of the blue circle equals the sum of the radii of the green and orange circles.
Python code
In case you’re interested, here’s the code that created the diagram.

#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script

# /// script
# dependencies = ["numpy", "matplotlib"]
# ///

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def connect(A, B, color='gray'):
    plt.plot([A[0], B[0]], [A[1], B[1]], color=color, linewidth=2)

def circle(c, r, color='gray'):
    t = np.linspace(0, 2*np.pi)
    plt.plot(c[0] + r*np.cos(t), c[1] + r*np.sin(t), color=color, linewidth=2)

def quadratic(a, b, c):
    det = b**2 - 4*a*c
    return ((-b - det**0.5)/(2*a), (-b + det**0.5)/(2*a))

A = np.array([-1, 0])
B = np.array([ 1, 0])
C = np.array([np.cos(1), np.sin(1)])
a = np.linalg.norm(B - C)
b = np.linalg.norm(A - C)
c = np.linalg.norm(B - A)
s = (a + b + c)/2

circle([0,0], 1)
connect(A, B,)
connect(A, C)
connect(C, B)
connect(C, C*np.array([1, -1]))

center = (a*A + b*B + c*C)/(2*s)
radius = 0.5*a*b/s
circle(center, radius, 'C0')

Ex = C[0]
roots = quadratic(1, 2 + 2*Ex, Ex**2 - 1)
r = roots[1] # Smaller root is negaive
print(roots)
center = (r + Ex, -r)
circle(center, r, 'C1')

roots = quadratic(1, 2 - 2*Ex, Ex**2 - 1)
r = roots[1] # Smaller root is negaive
center = (Ex - r, -r)
circle(center, r, 'C2')

plt.gca().set_aspect("equal")
plt.axis("off")
plt.show()
[1] Leon Bankoff. A Geometrical Coincidence. Mathematics Magazine, Vol. 37, No. 5 (Nov., 1964), p. 324.

对应该图的定理很有趣，但我发现复现这个图更有趣。
线段 AB 是一条直径，直线 CD 垂直于该直径。
假设外圆是一个单位圆。我猜测 C = (cos(1), sin(1))，并绘制了下图。
我是通过目测猜测 C 的值的，但回想起来，这可能是原图创作者为了方便而选择的一个值。
利用本文给出的圆心和半径方程，绘制三角形的内切蓝圆很容易。绘制另外两个圆（绿圆和橙圆）则比较困难。它们也是内切圆，但并非内切于三角形。它们内切于一个具有两条垂直边和一条圆弧的三边形。
绿圆的半径 r 是从圆心到其各切线的距离。此外，从原点到圆心的距离必须为 1 − r。这就足以建立一个关于 r 的二次方程。同样的推理也适用于橙圆。
原图来自文献 [1]，其阐述的定理指出：蓝圆的直径等于绿圆和橙圆的半径之和。
Python 代码
如果你感兴趣，这是绘制该图的代码。

#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script

# /// script
# dependencies = ["numpy", "matplotlib"]
# ///

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def connect(A, B, color='gray'):
    plt.plot([A[0], B[0]], [A[1], B[1]], color=color, linewidth=2)

def circle(c, r, color='gray'):
    t = np.linspace(0, 2*np.pi)
    plt.plot(c[0] + r*np.cos(t), c[1] + r*np.sin(t), color=color, linewidth=2)

def quadratic(a, b, c):
    det = b**2 - 4*a*c
    return ((-b - det**0.5)/(2*a), (-b + det**0.5)/(2*a))

A = np.array([-1, 0])
B = np.array([ 1, 0])
C = np.array([np.cos(1), np.sin(1)])
a = np.linalg.norm(B - C)
b = np.linalg.norm(A - C)
c = np.linalg.norm(B - A)
s = (a + b + c)/2

circle([0,0], 1)
connect(A, B,)
connect(A, C)
connect(C, B)
connect(C, C*np.array([1, -1]))

center = (a*A + b*B + c*C)/(2*s)
radius = 0.5*a*b/s
circle(center, radius, 'C0')

Ex = C[0]
roots = quadratic(1, 2 + 2*Ex, Ex**2 - 1)
r = roots[1] # Smaller root is negaive
print(roots)
center = (r + Ex, -r)
circle(center, r, 'C1')

roots = quadratic(1, 2 - 2*Ex, Ex**2 - 1)
r = roots[1] # Smaller root is negaive
center = (Ex - r, -r)
circle(center, r, 'C2')

plt.gca().set_aspect("equal")
plt.axis("off")
plt.show()
[1] Leon Bankoff. A Geometrical Coincidence. Mathematics Magazine, Vol. 37, No. 5 (Nov., 1964), p. 324.

articles.title: Amazon Basics, but for intellectual property.
articles.titleZh: 亚马逊基础版，但这次是针对知识产权的
articles.summary: 亚马逊屡次被指控利用其平台商家的数据来抄袭和自营产品，尽管官方始终否认任何不当行为。作为平台服务提供商，亚马逊掌握着所有产品的核心销售指标和用户数据，这使其在亲自下场销售产品时形成了巨大的利益冲突。凭借这种数据垄断优势，平台能够轻易识别爆款并推出类似“Amazon Basics”的自有品牌进行降维打击。这种既是裁判又是运动员的模式，严重威胁了第三方商家的知识产权和生存空间。
articles.summaryEn: Amazon has faced repeated accusations of ripping off merchants by using their platform data to create competing in-house products, allegations the company consistently denies. As the service provider, Amazon hosts all sales metrics and product data, creating a severe conflict of interest when it manufactures and sells its own goods. Leveraging this data monopoly, the platform can easily identify hit products and launch private labels like "Amazon Basics" to undercut original creators. This dual role as both referee and player severely threatens the intellectual property and survival of third-party merchants.
articles.reason: 深刻剖析了大型科技平台“既当裁判又当运动员”的数据垄断隐患，对关注平台经济和知识产权保护的读者极具启发性。

blocks.text: Amazon has been accused several times for ripping off merchants on its platform. And every single time they denied any wrongdoing.

A merchant, or anyone really, can create a product (or source it from China), then resell it on amazon. Amazon is the service provider, and hosts all the metrics concerning the products. If Amazon themselves were in the business of creating and selling products, then that creates a potential of conflict of interest. Because they have the data of all products that sell and sell well. They could replicate that success without doing any further research since the merchant has already confirmed the existence of demand.

It's not surprising that Amazon Basics quickly became the best selling "private-label brand" on Amazon. They already know what sells because they have access to the data. Yet they continued to deny it, and state that they only ever use publicly available data from sellers.

An Amazon spokesperson said the company believes the allegations are "factually incorrect and unsubstantiated," adding that Amazon strictly prohibits the "use or sharing of non-public, seller-specific data for the benefit of any seller, including sellers of private brands."
Yet the results are right there for all to see.

If you sell any product through Amazon, you are exposing your company's operations to them. If you want to keep that information to yourself, then you don't get to reach your customers, which in reality are Amazon's customers.

If you want to buy something online, and get it shipped as quickly as possible, then Amazon is a blessing. Most often than not, you are not buying the product directly from Amazon. An independent store or vendor with a presence on Amazon will fulfill your order. The seller only has minor identifying characteristics on the platform. On the search result page, the space designated to the seller is small and insignificant. The customer has very few reminders that products are offered by anyone but Amazon. (Although if you want to dispute a sale, you are starkly reminded that the item is from a 3rd party vendor.)

So there is no surprise when companies embrace AI internally, they are putting themselves at the risk of sharing their product with their competitors. Maybe the most obvious example is when Antropic came up with Claude Design. A tool to help users generate designs, wireframes, etc. Kinda like Figma.

That's not a problem on its own, but when Antropic's chief product officer sits on Figma's board of directors, you can't say that there isn't a conflict of interest there. In fact, the chief product officer resigned from the board merely days before Claude Design was announced. He basically extracted all value from Figma then resigned. Figma's AI features are built on top of Claude. So Anthropic literally pulled an Amazon Basic on Figma.

When companies force their own employees to use AI to do their day to day work, they are basically asking employees to upload company data to a 3rd party that may become a competitor. Sure something in the contract clause says that the AI company won't train on enterprise customer data, but nothing stops them from peaking at successful product data.

Whenever someone tells me that they used AI to build an app and boast of its values or uniqueness, I want to remind them that if you can just prompt-create a product, so can the AI provider. In fact, they might have better resources to create a competing product if it displays any sign of success (see Figma).

While it looks like plenty of people are benefitting from AI today, all this information is being shared with AI providers. We are giving them full access to our thought process. When you include them in your workflow, you are basically providing them with a step by step approach on how to do your job.
Don’t be surprised when you see a native Antropic/OpenAi project management application suite. Or a CRM, or any software that is trying to integrate with AI and may experience success.

A few years back, when I worked in Customer Service Automation, we discovered that most companies used Zendesk to manage their customer service. Since customers mainly contacted support via email, an intentional database had been built that tracked users through their shopping experience throughout the web.

While so much could be done with that data, like identifying “problematic” customers, or recommending products based on their history, we ended up finding something more helpful. We could easily detect a pattern of issues for certain shipping carriers. We could see when UPS was having delays in certain cities, or when Fedex was having technical issues when updating the last mile status. None of these things were features designed or provided by anyone. However, having access to businesses’ data gave us insight where we had none before.
That became a feature for us, only because we were not competitors to all these online retailers.
When you expose your company's internal data to a potential competitor, don’t be surprised when they build a competing business to rival you.

translations: 亚马逊曾多次被指控在其平台上剥削商家。而每一次他们都否认有任何不当行为。
商家，或者说任何人，都可以创建一个产品（或从中国进货），然后在亚马逊上转售。亚马逊作为服务提供商，掌握着与产品相关的所有指标数据。如果亚马逊自己也从事产品的创建和销售，就会产生潜在的利益冲突。因为他们拥有所有产品的销售数据，也知道哪些产品最畅销。既然商家已经确认了需求的存在，他们无需做任何进一步的研究就能复制这种成功。
Amazon Basics 迅速成为亚马逊上最畅销的“自有品牌”并不令人意外。因为可以访问这些数据，他们早就知道什么好卖。然而他们继续予以否认，并声称他们只使用卖家公开的数据。
亚马逊发言人表示，公司认为这些指控“在事实上是不正确且毫无根据的”，并补充说亚马逊严格禁止“为了任何卖家（包括自有品牌卖家）的利益而使用或共享非公开的特定卖家数据”。
然而，结果就明摆在那里，大家有目共睹。
如果你通过亚马逊销售任何产品，你就是在向他们暴露公司的运营状况。如果你想对这些信息保密，你就无法触达你的客户，而这些客户实际上是亚马逊的客户。
如果你想在网上买东西，并希望以最快的速度送达，那么亚马逊是个福音。但大多数时候，你并不是直接从亚马逊购买产品。你的订单通常是由在亚马逊上开店的独立商店或供应商履约的。卖家在该平台上只有极少的识别特征。在搜索结果页面上，留给卖家的空间微乎其微。客户几乎得不到任何提示，不知道这些产品是由亚马逊以外的任何人提供的。（不过，如果你想对某笔交易提出异议，系统会极其醒目地提醒你，该商品来自第三方供应商。）
因此，当公司在内部拥抱 AI 时，他们实际上正将自己置于与竞争对手共享自家产品的风险之中，这毫不令人意外。也许最明显的例子就是 Anthropic 推出的 Claude Design。这是一个帮助用户生成设计、线框图等的工具，有点像 Figma。

这本身并不是问题，但当 Anthropic 的首席产品官同时兼任 Figma 的董事会成员时，你就不能说这里不存在利益冲突了。事实上，这位首席产品官在 Claude Design 发布的几天前才辞去了董事会职务。他基本上是从 Figma 榨取了所有价值，然后辞职走人。Figma 的 AI 功能是建立在 Claude 之上的。所以，Anthropic 简直是对 Figma 玩了一出 Amazon Basics 的戏码。
当公司强制员工使用 AI 来完成日常工作时，他们基本上是在要求员工将公司数据上传给可能成为竞争对手的第三方。当然，合同条款中可能会规定 AI 公司不会使用企业客户的数据进行训练，但并没有什么能阻止他们偷看成功产品的数据。
每当有人告诉我他们使用 AI 构建了一个应用程序，并吹嘘其价值或独特性时，我都想提醒他们：既然你能通过提示词创建一个产品，AI 提供商也能做到。事实上，如果这个产品展现出任何成功的迹象，他们可能会拥有更好的资源来打造一款竞争产品（参考 Figma 的例子）。
尽管如今似乎许多人都从 AI 中获益，但所有这些信息都在与 AI 提供商共享。我们等于赋予了他们完全窥探我们思考过程的权限。当你在工作流中引入 AI 时，你本质上就是在向他们提供一份手把手教你如何工作的指南。
当你看到 Antropic 或 OpenAI 推出原生的项目管理应用套件时，大可不必感到惊讶。或者是 CRM 系统，又或者是任何试图集成 AI 并有望取得成功的软件，情况也是如此。
几年前，我在从事客服自动化工作时发现，大多数公司都在使用 Zendesk 来管理客户服务。由于客户主要通过电子邮件联系技术支持，我们便建立了一个专门的数据库，用于在全网范围内追踪用户的购物体验。
尽管这些数据能用于很多事情，比如识别“问题”客户，或是根据用户历史记录推荐产品，但我们最终发现了更具实用价值的用途。我们能够轻松检测出特定物流承运商的故障模式。我们可以确切知道 UPS 在哪些城市出现了延误，或者 FedEx 在更新“最后一公里”状态时何时发生了技术故障。这些洞察并非由任何人专门设计或作为功能提供。然而，仅仅是因为接触到了这些业务数据，我们就获得了前所未有的视角。
之所以这能成为我们的一项特色功能，仅仅是因为我们与这些在线零售商并非竞争对手。
当你将公司的内部数据暴露给潜在竞争对手时，如果他们顺势建立起一项业务来与你抗衡，请不要感到惊讶。

articles.title: Jason Snell Ends His Column, and 28-Year Run, at Macworld
articles.titleZh: Jason Snell 结束了他在 Macworld 长达 28 年的专栏作家生涯
articles.summary: 资深科技记者 Jason Snell 正式结束了他在科技媒体 Macworld 长达 28 年的专栏作家生涯。他回忆了自己 1997 年秋天入职时的场景，当时的苹果正处于破产边缘，史蒂夫·乔布斯刚刚回归并驱逐了时任 CEO。在那个还没有 iMac 和可见产品线复苏迹象的艰难时刻，苹果的生存命悬一线，乔布斯只能请求大众给予信任。这段跨越近三十年的专栏历史，见证了苹果从濒临倒闭到重塑科技辉煌的完整历程。
articles.summaryEn: Veteran tech journalist Jason Snell has officially concluded his 28-year run as a columnist for Macworld. He recalls starting his job in the fall of 1997, a time when Apple was on the brink of bankruptcy and Steve Jobs had just returned to oust the sitting CEO. During those challenging times, before the iMac or any visible product turnaround existed, Apple's survival hung by a thread while Jobs asked the public for trust. This retiring column represents a near-thirty-year historical record that witnessed Apple's complete journey from near collapse to technological dominance.
articles.reason: 以一位资深科技记者亲历者的独特视角，浓缩了苹果公司从濒死边缘到重返巅峰的波澜壮阔的科技史。

blocks.text: My first day on the job at Macworld, Apple was perilously close to going out of business. It was the fall of 1997, and Steve Jobs had returned to Apple and engineered the ejection of Gil Amelio as CEO, but there was no iMac yet, no visible turnaround in terms of products at all. Beyond the release of the iconic “Think Different” ad campaign, there was nothing.

Apple’s survival hung by a thread. Steve Jobs asked everyone to trust him. At Macworld Expo, he had enlisted Bill Gates–Bill Gates, of all people!–to help him instill belief in the world that Apple would find a way to survive.

The world was skeptical, to say the least. My family asked what job I thought I’d get once Apple went out of business. The magazine I had worked at for four years, MacUser, had folded, and some of us had been transferred over to our rival, Macworld, presumably to publish issues until Apple finally gave up the ghost and died. We existed to minimize the loss exposure of our respective publishing companies.
1997 was weird, folks. And that’s how my tenure at Macworld started.
It got better

Of course, in 1998, Apple announced and shipped the iMac, and its fortunes began to turn around. Mac OS X finally appeared in the early 2000s, and it is still the foundation of every device Apple makes. Somehow, Apple found a way to fashion a new Mac OS out of NeXTSTEP while maintaining enough Mac compatibility to keep users and software developers on the platform–a magic trick that I still don’t think gets enough credit in Apple’s turnaround.

Covering Apple during the first decade of this century was like blasting off into space on a rocket. In a breathtakingly short amount of time, doom and gloom were replaced by a rain of improbable success stories, from the iPod to the revitalization of the Mac to the success of Apple retail stores to the really big one, the iPhone.
The author (highlighted) at the iPod launch in 2001.
Foundry

But every story, even the really good ones, ends eventually. Steve Jobs’s illness and death happened just as his utter triumph with the iPhone had become apparent. At the time, again, the consensus was that Apple was in deep trouble without its leader at the helm. And once again, those who were skeptical about the future of Apple were proven to be wrong. Really wrong.

The Tim Cook era was–it feels a little weird to start using that in the past tense, but here we are–all about growth. Cook was never going to be Steve Jobs, and to his credit, he never tried to be. Cook’s successes are all about managing the unprecedented growth and success of Apple’s products, driven primarily by the incredible popularity of the iPhone.

In hindsight, it was the perfect match of the man to the moment: Cook’s entire being seems focused on keeping the supply chain humming, innovating in manufacturing processes, and pressing the advantage with in-demand products. Cook led Apple through a period when it could’ve fumbled its opportunity with the iPhone, and there was no fumbling to be seen.

The moment the iPhone really took off and went exponential was in September 2014, when the iPhone 6 and 6 Plus signaled Apple’s embrace of the larger phone styles that Samsung had proved were appealing to consumers. It’s also probably the moment Cook is most proud of, because it also marked the launch of the Apple Watch, the most consequential new product released during Cook’s tenure.
The next chapter

It seems like my own personal milestones tend to happen alongside Apple’s pivot points. I arrived at Macworld when Apple was lost, and I departed just as it zoomed further into the stratosphere. The day after Apple launched the iPhone 6 and Apple Watch was my last day as a full-time employee at Macworld.

Fortunately, I had time to prepare, so I launched Six Colors, where I’ve been writing about Apple ever since. And Jon Phillips and the other excellent people at Macworld immediately asked me to come back and write More Color starting in early 2015. In my Macworld afterlife as a contributor, I’ve turned in nearly 500 columns over the last 11 years, extending the presence of my Macworld tenure to 29 years.

We’re at a new pivot point now. And while I’ve spoken to Tim Cook a total of one time–I said hello at WWDC 2026 because he sat down right in front of me at the company’s live AI “tech talk”–I’ve talked to incoming CEO John Ternus a lot. He’s different from Cook in so many ways, and that’s a good thing. Apple has been incredibly successful for a long time, and when you’re that successful, it makes it easy to ignore organizational problems or blind spots, because why mess with a good thing?

Ternus doesn’t need to use a wrecking ball on Apple, and he won’t, but he has the opportunity to survey how the company does business and make needed changes. He’s been at Apple for a quarter of a century, rising up in the hardware group over the years; surely, along the way, he’s noticed a lot of things that Apple could change and improve on.

In fact, that brings up what makes me most enthusiastic about Ternus coming in as CEO. Tim Cook is a business-school guy who was recruited by Steve Jobs because Apple desperately needed someone who could create a disciplined supply chain and manufacturing organization. That wasn’t Jobs’s forte, so he made a great hire in Cook. But while Cook seems to have truly embraced Apple and what makes it special, he’s always been a high-level exec focused on specific areas of Apple’s business.

Ternus isn’t like that. He’s a lifer at Apple. He came in at the ground level. He is one of us, at least in the sense that I think he viscerally understands what makes Apple’s products appeal to its customer base. He’s been closer to the nuts and bolts of what makes Apple work than Cook ever was. Having a CEO with that perspective will be good for Apple, at a time when the company seems to have conquered the world–but is now struggling to adapt to some rapid changes in the tech industry.
With his appearance on March 19, 2026, Jason Snell became the third Macworld contributor to have been a contestant on Jeopardy! (Glenn Fleishman and Dan Moren are the other two.)
Jason Snell

A new pivot point for Apple? Seems like a good time for a new pivot for me, too. This year has been full of milestones for me, from appearing on “Jeopardy!” to reviewing David Pogue’s book about Apple for The Wall Street Journal, to crowdfunding a new podcast about Apple history. Along the way, I’ve had to say goodbye to some longstanding projects.

That’s my long way of saying that this is my last More Color column at Macworld. Thank you so much to everyone at Macworld for the chance to keep my name attached to this brand for an additional 11 years on top of the 17 I spent in my first life as an editor. Thanks to my editor, Roman Loyola, who was already working at MacUser magazine on my first day there in 1994 and is somehow still working with me. And thanks to all of you for reading my words here over the years. I’ll keep bleeding six colors, and I know that you will, too.

translations: 我在 Macworld 上班的第一天，Apple 正处于濒临破产的边缘。那是 1997 年秋天，Steve Jobs 已经重返 Apple 并策划赶走了当时的 CEO Gil Amelio，但那时 iMac 尚未问世，产品方面完全看不到任何转机。除了发布那支标志性的“Think Different”广告活动外，再无其他动作。
Apple 的生存命悬一线。Steve Jobs 请求所有人相信他。在 Macworld Expo 上，他甚至拉来了 Bill Gates——竟然是 Bill Gates！——来帮助他向全世界注入 Apple 必将找到生存之道的信念。
往轻了说，整个世界都对此持怀疑态度。我的家人问我，觉得等 Apple 破产后我能找到什么样的工作。我效力了四年的杂志《MacUser》已经停刊，我们中的一些人被调到了竞争对手 Macworld 那里，大概是为了在 Apple 最终咽下最后一口气、彻底倒闭之前继续出版杂志吧。我们的存在，仅仅是为了将各自出版公司的损失风险降到最低。
各位，1997 年就是这么古怪。而这就是我在 Macworld 职业生涯的开端。
情况开始好转

当然，在 1998 年，Apple 发布并推出了 iMac，其命运开始逆转。Mac OS X 终于在 2000 年代初问世，并且至今仍是 Apple 制造的每一款设备的基石。Apple 竟然找到了一种方法，用 NeXTSTEP 打造出一个全新的 Mac OS，同时保持了足够的 Mac 兼容性，从而将用户和软件开发者留在了这个平台上——这一魔术般的壮举，我至今仍认为它在 Apple 的绝地反击中没有得到足够的赞誉。
在本世纪的头十年里，报道 Apple 就像是乘坐火箭升入太空。在短得令人惊叹的时间里，厄运和阴霾被一连串不可思议的成功奇迹所取代，从 iPod 到 Mac 的复兴，再到 Apple 零售店的成功，直至最后的大赢家——iPhone。
2001 年 iPod 发布会上的作者（高亮处）。
Foundry
但每个故事，哪怕是再精彩的故事，最终都会迎来结局。Steve Jobs 的病情恶化与离世，恰好发生在他凭借 iPhone 取得彻底胜利变得显而易见的时刻。当时，人们的共识再次倾向于：失去了掌舵的领袖，Apple 陷入了巨大的麻烦。然而，那些对 Apple 未来持怀疑态度的人再一次被证明是错的。错得离谱。
Tim Cook 时代——现在开始用过去时来谈论它感觉有点奇怪，但事实就是如此——完全是关于增长的。Cook 永远成不了 Steve Jobs，而且值得称赞的是，他也从未想过要成为 Jobs。Cook 的成功之处在于成功驾驭了 Apple 产品前所未有的增长与成功，而这主要得益于 iPhone 令人难以置信的受欢迎程度。
回想起来，这是一个人与时代的完美契合：Cook 的全部精力似乎都集中在保持供应链的高效运转、创新制造工艺，以及利用热门产品扩大优势上。Cook 带领 Apple 度过了一个本可能错失 iPhone 机遇的时期，而没有出现任何闪失。
iPhone 真正起飞并呈现指数级增长的时刻是在 2014 年 9 月，当时 iPhone 6 和 6 Plus 标志着 Apple 开始拥抱 Samsung 已证明对消费者极具吸引力的大屏手机风格。这可能也是 Cook 最引以为傲的时刻，因为它同时也标志着 Apple Watch 的发布，这是 Cook 任期内发布的意义最重大的新产品。
新的篇章
似乎我个人的重要里程碑总是与 Apple 的转折点相伴而生。我在 Apple 迷失方向时加入了 Macworld，而在它一飞冲天之际离开了那里。Apple 发布 iPhone 6 和 Apple Watch 的第二天，正是我在 Macworld 担任全职员工的最后一天。
幸运的是，我有时间做准备，所以我创办了 Six Colors，从那以后我就一直在那里撰写关于 Apple 的文章。Jon Phillips 和 Macworld 的其他优秀同仁立刻邀请我回归，从 2015 年初开始撰写《More Color》专栏。在离开 Macworld 后作为撰稿人的岁月里，过去 11 年间我提交了近 500 篇专栏文章，将我与 Macworld 的渊源延续到了 29 年。

我们现在正处于一个新的转折点。虽然我和 Tim Cook 总共只说过一次话——那是在 WWDC 2026 上，因为他在公司举办的 AI 现场“技术讲座”中刚好坐在我正前方，我向他打了个招呼——但我却和即将接任 CEO 的 John Ternus 交流过很多次。他在很多方面都和 Cook 不同，这是一件好事。Apple 很长一段时间以来都取得了难以置信的成功，而当你如此成功时，很容易忽视组织内部的问题或盲区，因为既然现状大好，又何必折腾呢？
Ternus 不需要对 Apple 进行大动干戈的破坏，他也不会这么做，但他有机会审视公司的运营方式并做出必要的改变。他已经在 Apple 待了四分之一个世纪，这些年来在硬件部门不断晋升；可以肯定的是，在这一路走来的过程中，他已经注意到了许多 Apple 可以改变和改进的地方。

事实上，这也引出了最让我对 Ternus 接任 CEO 感到兴奋的地方。Tim Cook 是个拥有商学院背景的人，Steve Jobs 当年招募他，是因为 Apple 极其需要有人能建立起纪律严明的供应链和制造体系。这并不是 Jobs 的强项，所以他招到了 Cook 这员大将。但是，尽管 Cook 似乎已经真正融入了 Apple 并理解其独特之处，但他始终是一位专注于 Apple 业务特定领域的高管。
Ternus 则不同。他是一位终身效力于 Apple 的人。他从基层做起。他是我们中的一员，至少我认为，他从骨子里明白是什么让 Apple 的产品对客户群体产生如此大的吸引力。相比于 Cook，他更贴近 Apple 得以运转的核心细节。在公司似乎已经征服了世界、但如今正努力适应科技行业快速变化之际，拥有一位具备这种视角的 CEO 将对 Apple 大有裨益。
随着 Jason Snell 在 2026 年 3 月 19 日登台亮相，他成为了第三位曾作为选手参加《Jeopardy!》智力竞赛节目的 Macworld 撰稿人（另外两位是 Glenn Fleishman 和 Dan Moren）。
Jason Snell
Apple 迎来了新的转折点？对我而言，似乎也是开启新转折的好时机。今年对我来说充满了里程碑式的事件，从参加《Jeopardy!》节目，到为《华尔街日报》撰写 David Pogue 关于 Apple 的新书书评，再到为一个关于 Apple 历史的新播客发起众筹。与此同时，我也不得不告别一些长期进行的项目。

绕了这么大一个圈子，其实我是想说，这是我在 Macworld 撰写的最后一篇 More Color 专栏。非常感谢 Macworld 的所有同仁，让我有机会在第一段 17 年编辑生涯的基础之上，又让我的名字与这个品牌继续相伴了 11 年。感谢我的编辑 Roman Loyola，1994 年我入职 MacUser 杂志的第一天他就在那里工作，而不知怎么地，我们至今仍在并肩作战。也要感谢这些年来在这里阅读我文章的所有读者。我会继续为六色苹果倾注热血，我知道你们也一样。

articles.title: e approximation
articles.titleZh: 自然常数 e 的分数近似值
articles.summary: 数学常数 e 存在一个精度极高的有理数近似值：2721/1001。与直接截断小数位的简单做法（如 2718/1000 仅能提供四位有效数字精度）相比，2721/1001 在分母大小相近的情况下，能够将精度大幅提升至七位，甚至接近八位有效数字。这种相对于其分母规模而言异常出色的逼近能力，展示了有理数在数值计算中的奇妙特性。该发现为需要快速计算且对精度有要求的算法场景提供了一种极其高效的替代方案。
articles.summaryEn: The mathematical constant e has a highly accurate rational approximation: 2721/1001. Compared to the trivial method of truncating decimals (such as 2718/1000, which only provides four significant figures), 2721/1001 achieves seven, almost eight, significant figures of accuracy with a similarly sized denominator. This remarkable precision relative to the size of its denominator showcases the fascinating properties of rational numbers in numerical computations. This finding provides a highly efficient alternative for algorithmic scenarios requiring fast computations and strict precision.
articles.reason: 用极其直观的数学案例展示了有理数逼近的神奇精度，对算法工程师和数学爱好者来说是个有趣的实用技巧。

fullText.siteName: John D. Cook | Applied Mathematics Consulting

blocks.text: I ran across the approximation
recently. What makes this remarkable is its accuracy relative to the size of the denominator.
You can create a trivial approximation just by truncating a decimal expansion
but this is only good to four significant figures, but 2721/1001 is good to seven, almost eight, significant figures.
The comparison is more impressive in binary.
The denominator is a 10-bit number but the approximation is accurate to 21 bits.

articles.title: Why IBM bought Lotus
articles.summary: 1995 年 7 月 6 日，IBM 以 35 亿美元的价格收购了 Lotus Development 公司。Lotus 曾是全球第二大软件发行商，其 IPO 时的估值高达 55 亿美元，核心王牌产品是 Lotus 1-2-3 电子表格软件。这桩世纪收购反映了当时个人电脑软件市场的激烈竞争，以及 IBM 试图在软件生态中建立企业级护城河的战略意图。随着微软 Office 的强势崛起，Lotus 的辉煌逐渐落幕，但此次收购深刻影响了现代企业级协同软件的发展格局。
articles.summaryEn: On July 6, 1995, IBM acquired Lotus Development for $3.5 billion. Lotus was once the second largest software publisher in the world, boasting a valuation of $5.5 billion at its IPO, largely driven by its flagship spreadsheet product, Lotus 1-2-3. This monumental acquisition reflected the fierce competition in the PC software market and IBM's strategic intent to build an enterprise moat in the software ecosystem. Although Lotus's glory eventually faded with the rise of Microsoft Office, this buyout profoundly reshaped the landscape of modern enterprise collaboration software.
articles.reason: 带领读者回顾科技史上的一桩经典并购案，对理解软件行业的周期性兴衰和企业级市场的战略布局具有重要借鉴意义。

blocks.text: On July 6, 1995, IBM bought Lotus Development for $3.5 billion. Lotus had once been the second largest software publisher in the world and was worth $5.5 billion at its IPO. Its flagship product, the spreadsheet Lotus 1-2-3, had been a key driver in sales of the original IBM PC in the early 1980s. By 1995, Lotus wasn’t trending in the right direction, but IBM had plans and thought Lotus fit into them.
What IBM saw in Lotus

In 1995, IBM still had designs on competing with Microsoft head-on. IBM had operating systems and a database, but they were lacking in the applications software department, both on the desktop and on the server. Lotus had the #3 office suite, behind Microsoft Office and Novell’s Perfect Office. But the key was Lotus’ e-mail/backoffice server called Domino, and a client for it called Notes. Domino was doing what Sharepoint and Exchange do now, but it was doing it in the mid 90s.
Meanwhile, Novell had been doing similar things, building up a collection of software to go head to head with Microsoft. IBM couldn’t compete alone, but with Lotus they could.
How they fit together

In the Computer Chronicles episode covering COMDEX 1994 that aired September 5, 1994, IBM’s Lee Reiswig said OS/2 delivered everything Windows 95 was promising and everything Windows NT had wanted to be, and that you could buy it right then.

The problem was native 32-bit software. You could run 16 bit Windows applications on OS/2, but you didn’t get the full benefit unless you were running native 32-bit software, just like the Windows platforms. Lotus had 32-bit OS/2 versions of its office suite, its Notes client, and Domino server, but didn’t really promote it.

Buying Lotus gave IBM options. In June 1995, Windows 95’s release was no longer a distant thing. Everyone knew Windows 95 and Office 95 would debut near the end of the summer. Everyone knew they would sell well. What wasn’t certain yet was how well it would work once it got into the hands of millions of consumers. There was still a little bit of doubt about it, the possibility that it would go in the direction that Windows Vista later did, being too slow for current hardware, or in the direction that Windows ME did, being too unstable.

If that happened, IBM could pitch OS/2 and Smartsuite as the smarter alternative. That didn’t happen, and  consumers overwhelmingly opted for Windows 95. But IBM still found a willing audience in the business market.
Selling the IBM-Lotus software stack to businesses

Businesses tend to adopt new operating systems more slowly than consumers do. While many businesses did indeed adopt Windows 95, OS/2 and Smartsuite did do well for several years in the business market. I know from experience. In 1998, I was miserable in my job, but I had a couple of years of experience with both Windows NT 4.0 and OS/2. I could still find OS/2 jobs to apply for in 1998, partly because OS/2 ran better on laptops than NT 4 did. NT had no power management to speak of, so OS/2 offered the stability of NT and the battery life of Win95.
I wonder a lot what would have happened if I had taken one of those jobs instead of doing what I did, but I digress.

And with control of Lotus, IBM could ensure the continued availability of the key software it needed to sell into that market, regardless of what the consumer world did. Meanwhile, IBM could sell Lotus software into Microsoft shops as well. Accounting departments liked having Lotus 1-2-3 because it was familiar, and Notes and Domino were useful regardless of whether you ran them on Windows, OS/2, AIX (IBM’s Unix), or any combination of them. In a mixed environment, IBM could thrive. And being a large corporation, IBM understood that large businesses tended to migrate slowly.

IBM even went so far as to offer native versions of Notes and Domino for Windows NT 4.0 running on DEC’s Alpha CPU. While Microsoft pushed Windows running on x86, that left plenty of niches for IBM to find and sell into, and they did. Even when it meant compiling for a CPU that competed with IBM’s own PowerPC CPU.
This idea would have been ludicrous in 1992. But under Lou Gerstner, IBM no longer insisted on selling you the whole product stack.
Thriving in niches

IBM and Lotus thrived in niches, even as the opportunity for mainstream success withered away. Domino was a million times better than Exchange, but Exchange and Outlook worked with cool toys that its client, Lotus Notes, didn’t. Domino’s momentum didn’t go away all at once, but trendy turn-of-the-century gadgets steadily eroded it.

Exchange and Outlook worked just fine with a Palm Pilot. It took IBM forever to get Notes working with a Palm Pilot, and once they did, the cool thing was a Blackberry. The cool toys worked with Exchange, so Notes got relegated to legacy things. Companies that had Notes and had used it for e-mail would inevitably build other corporate intranet applications with it as well. And once they had migrated off to Exchange, there was always something that worked under Notes and had no equivalent under SharePoint.

IBM guessed correctly that Lotus Notes would be sticky like IBM’s mainframes. But IBM wasn’t able to use that to hold onto the rest of the market. Nor was it able to turn those niches where Notes stuck into a growth market. Domino looked like a redundant system running next to Microsoft technologies. And when you’re a redundant system, every incoming CIO wants to cut you out. Even when that fails, you probably won’t be selling many upgrades.
Lotus and IBM: Unhappy together

Lotus never seemed to especially like being part of IBM. This was visible at conferences, where Lotus employees would cross out IBM on their badges and write in “Lotus.” But there isn’t much reason to believe they would have done much better on their own. The momentum was on Microsoft’s side long before IBM acquired Lotus. In 2018, IBM sold what was left of Lotus to HCL, an India-based software conglomerate, for $1.8 billion.
Buying Lotus wasn’t a mistake
My contrarian view is that IBM buying Lotus wasn’t a mistake. Hear me out.

IBM was placing a bet with Lotus. And it’s easy to look at the $3.5 billion that IBM paid for Lotus versus the $1.8 billion IBM sold Lotus for, and say IBM lost. But in the early years, IBM was turning profits of $1-2 billion in software per quarter, and Lotus Notes was a big part of that. The $1.7 billion that IBM lost on Lotus represents one quarter’s worth of software profits from the 90s.

IBM’s Lotus acquisition represents a merger of two past-their-prime companies. The union didn’t return either of them to their early 1980s heights and it’s tempting to think Win95-era Microsoft smashed them like a bug. But that’s a massive oversimplification that ignores a decade of IBM and Lotus quietly doing better together in Microsoft’s shadow than most of us remember. And if Microsoft had timed its missteps a bit differently, it’s possible the Lotus acquisition could have yielded a few more good years than it did.

David Farquhar is a computer security professional, entrepreneur, and author. He has written professionally about computers since 1991, so he was writing about retro computers when they were still new. He has been working in IT professionally since 1994 and has specialized in vulnerability management since 2013. He holds Security+ and CISSP certifications. Today he blogs five times a week, mostly about retro computers and retro gaming covering the time period from 1975 to 2000.

translations: 1995年7月6日，IBM以35亿美元收购了Lotus Development。Lotus曾经是全球第二大软件发行商，在首次公开募股（IPO）时的市值高达55亿美元。其旗舰产品、电子表格软件 Lotus 1-2-3 曾是20世纪80年代初初代 IBM PC 销量的关键驱动力。到1995年时，Lotus 的势头已经不太好，但 IBM 早有计划，并认为 Lotus 非常契合其战略布局。
IBM 看中了 Lotus 的什么

1995年，IBM 依然打算与 Microsoft 展开正面竞争。IBM 拥有操作系统和数据库，但在桌面端和服务器端的应用软件领域存在短板。Lotus 拥有排名第三的办公套件，仅次于 Microsoft Office 和 Novell 的 Perfect Office。但关键在于 Lotus 名为 Domino 的电子邮件/后台服务器，以及名为 Notes 的客户端。Domino 在90年代中期就已经实现了如今 Sharepoint 和 Exchange 的功能。
与此同时，Novell 也在做着类似的事情，构建了一套软件组合来与 Microsoft 正面交锋。IBM 无法单凭一己之力竞争，但有了 Lotus 的加入，他们就能做到。
它们是如何契合的
在1994年9月5日播出的报道1994年 COMDEX 展会的《计算机编年史》（Computer Chronicles）节目中，IBM 的 Lee Reiswig 表示，OS/2 已经实现了 Windows 95 所承诺的一切以及 Windows NT 想要达到的所有目标，而且当时就可以买得到。
问题在于原生32位软件。你可以在 OS/2 上运行16位 Windows 应用程序，但除非你运行的是原生32位软件，否则无法获得全部优势，这与 Windows 平台是一样的。Lotus 的办公套件、Notes 客户端和 Domino 服务器都有32位版的 OS/2 版本，但并没有真正进行推广。

收购 Lotus 为 IBM 提供了更多选择。在1995年6月，Windows 95 的发布已经指日可待。大家都知道 Windows 95 和 Office 95 将在夏末亮相，也都知道它们会大卖。但当时尚不确定的是，一旦它们交到数百万消费者手中，实际运行效果会怎样。人们对此仍存有一些疑虑：它有可能走上后来 Windows Vista 的老路，在当时的硬件上运行过于缓慢；或者像 Windows ME 那样，系统极不稳定。
如果真的发生这种情况，IBM 就可以将 OS/2 和 Smartsuite 作为更明智的选择进行推销。不过这种情况并未发生，消费者压倒性地选择了 Windows 95。但 IBM 依然在企业市场找到了愿意接受其产品的受众。
向企业推销 IBM-Lotus 软件栈

企业采用新操作系统的速度往往比消费者慢。尽管许多企业确实采用了 Windows 95，但 OS/2 和 Smartsuite 在企业市场确实有过几年的辉煌时期。这是我的经验之谈。1998年，我的工作很不顺心，但我已经拥有了几年使用 Windows NT 4.0 和 OS/2 的经验。在1998年，我依然能找到需要 OS/2 技能的工作机会，部分原因是 OS/2 在笔记本电脑上的运行效果比 NT 4 更好。NT 几乎没有任何电源管理功能，因此 OS/2 既提供了 NT 的稳定性，又具备了 Win95 的电池续航能力。
我经常在想，如果当初我接受了其中一份工作，而不是走了现在的路，会发生什么，不过这扯远了。

通过控制 Lotus，IBM 能够确保其打入该市场所需的关键软件持续可用，无论消费领域发生什么变化。与此同时，IBM 还可以将 Lotus 软件销售给微软的客户群。财务部门喜欢使用 Lotus 1-2-3，因为它广为人知；而无论你是在 Windows、OS/2、AIX（IBM 的 Unix）还是它们的任意组合上运行，Notes 和 Domino 都非常实用。在混合环境中，IBM 能够蓬勃发展。并且，作为一家大公司，IBM 深知大型企业的迁移过程往往十分缓慢。
IBM 甚至专门为运行在 DEC 的 Alpha CPU 上的 Windows NT 4.0 提供了原生版本的 Notes 和 Domino。虽然微软大力推广运行在 x86 上的 Windows，但这为 IBM 留下了大量可以发掘并推销产品的利基市场，而且他们也确实做到了。即使这意味着要为与 IBM 自家的 PowerPC CPU 竞争的 CPU 进行编译。
这种想法在 1992 年看来简直荒谬。但在郭士纳（Lou Gerstner）的领导下，IBM 不再坚持向客户出售整个产品栈。
在利基市场中蓬勃发展
IBM 和 Lotus 在利基市场中蓬勃发展，尽管主流市场成功的机会正在逐渐消失。Domino 比 Exchange 好上一百万倍，但 Exchange 和 Outlook 能够与各种新潮设备配合使用，而其客户端 Lotus Notes 却不能。Domino 的发展势头并没有立即消退，但世纪之交的那些时髦设备却在稳步地侵蚀着它。

Exchange 和 Outlook 与 Palm Pilot 配合得非常好。IBM 花了很长时间才让 Notes 能够在 Palm Pilot 上运行，而等他们做到时，酷炫的设备已经变成了黑莓（Blackberry）。这些新潮设备都能与 Exchange 兼容，因此 Notes 被降级成了老旧的遗留系统。那些拥有 Notes 并将其用于电子邮件的公司，不可避免地也会用它来构建其他的企业内部网应用。而一旦他们迁移到 Exchange，总会发现某些在 Notes 下运行的功能在 SharePoint 中找不到对应的替代品。
IBM 猜对了，Lotus Notes 会像 IBM 的大型机一样具有用户粘性。但 IBM 无法利用这一点来保住其余的市场份额，也无法将 Notes 盘踞的这些利基市场转化为增长型市场。Domino 看起来就像是一个运行在微软技术旁边的冗余系统。而当你成为一个冗余系统时，每一任新上任的 CIO 都想将你淘汰出局。即使淘汰失败，你可能也卖不出多少次升级了。
Lotus 与 IBM：不愉快的结合
Lotus 似乎从来都不怎么喜欢成为 IBM 的一部分。这在会议上显而易见，Lotus 的员工会划掉他们胸牌上的 IBM，并写上“Lotus”。但我们没有太多理由相信，如果他们独立发展，情况会好多少。早在 IBM 收购 Lotus 之前，微软就已经占据了发展势头。2018 年，IBM 将 Lotus 的剩余资产以 18 亿美元的价格出售给了印度软件企业集团 HCL。
收购 Lotus 并非一个错误
我的唱反调的观点是，IBM 收购 Lotus 并不是一个错误。请听我把话说完。
IBM 收购 Lotus 是在押注。人们很容易盯着 IBM 收购 Lotus 花费的 35 亿美元与卖出时的 18 亿美元，然后断言 IBM 亏了。但在最初几年里，IBM 每季度的软件利润高达 10 到 20 亿美元，而 Lotus Notes 在其中占了很大比重。IBM 在 Lotus 身上损失的这 17 亿美元，其实仅相当于其 90 年代一个季度的软件利润。

IBM 收购 Lotus 是两家已过巅峰期的公司之间的合并。这次联姻并未让它们重回 20 世纪 80 年代初的巅峰，人们很容易认为是 Win95 时代的微软像踩死虫子一样把它们碾碎了。但这是一种严重的过度简化，它忽略了在微软的阴影下，IBM 和 Lotus 在长达十年的时间里携手取得了远超我们记忆的出色业绩。而且，如果微软在失误的时机上稍有不同，收购 Lotus 本可能会带来比实际情况多几年的好光景。
